label: a6-thm-derivative-of-an-inverse
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: All boundary cases are correctly handled or explicitly excluded. The interval I is required to be nondegenerate (at least two points), ensuring every point is a limit point and derivatives are meaningful. Endpoints are included – the limit-point argument (L3) works for all points of an order-convex set with at least two points, so one‑sided derivatives at endpoints are properly captured. The case f'(c)=0 is treated separately by chain‑rule contradiction, and f'(c)≠0 uses Carathéodory’s factorisation with division by the nowhere‑zero factor φ∘g. No division by zero occurs where it is not allowed; the algebra of continuous functions is applied only after verifying the denominator is non‑vanishing on the whole domain. The proof never assumes compactness or boundedness. No counterexample exists under the stated hypotheses – the theorem is the standard inverse‑function‑rule plus the known obstruction at a horizontal tangent.

SOURCES: Every supplied cited item used by the target was inspected: def‑derivative, thm‑caratheodory‑characterisation, thm‑chain‑rule, thm‑continuous‑inverse, def‑continuity‑real, def‑injection‑surjection‑bijection, def‑interval, thm‑algebra‑of‑continuous‑functions, thm‑composition‑of‑continuous‑functions, def‑function‑limit, def‑limit‑point‑r, cor‑of‑one‑positive. Each supplies the exact property required by the proof without mismatch.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered proof step (1.1–6.1), and the Remarks have been examined.
